component.name: Honeycomb
component.summary: Keep a calm blood glucose journal

description.p: Honeycomb is a journal for blood glucose readings. Open it and the reading field is ready: type a number, press Enter, and it is saved with the time and, if you like, whether it was fasting, before or after a meal, or at bedtime. The app says whether a reading is in range, high or low in plain words, and nothing nags.

Trends shows your average, time in range, estimated A1c and variability over a week, a month or any dates you pick, compared with the period before, along with charts of every reading, the daily average and the time of day your levels run high. The report page turns the same figures into a clean sheet for your doctor that you can print, save as a PDF or export as CSV.

Readings are kept in a plain CSV file you own. Pair your computers and the Honeycomb Android app to keep them in step: devices talk to each other directly with end-to-end encryption, with no account and no server holding your data.
Estimated A1c is calculated from your readings and is not a laboratory result. Talk to your care team about your targets.

description.p: Honeycomb is ready to run as a Flatpak. Inside one, updates arrive through Flatpak and opening the app again brings back the window that is already running.

Deleting a reading from its edit dialog works again. Saving is safer: edits made to the data file by hand are kept, a file that briefly goes missing is written back rather than emptied, and quitting waits for the last save to finish.
The Android app opens again. Desktop builds carry only the version change.
Trends has a daily average chart, with each day's readings joined into one line on the same target band, so the direction over a few weeks is easy to see.
Honeycomb runs on Windows. Automatic update checks, when turned on, repeat every twelve hours while the app is open.
The report lists the newest readings first, the same order as the Log page.

Sync no longer loses a reading saved while another device is syncing, and devices only exchange readings when something changed. A phone can pair by scanning a QR code, and a dated backup of the data file is kept before each day's first change.
Links in About open in the browser, and the Devices and About sections are better spaced.
Controls are easier to read in light mode, and Settings has an About section.
Trends and the report can step back through earlier periods, and the latest readings are always in view.
